spec.title: Add documentation browser TreeView sections to sidebar
spec.context:
Existing product and engineering documentation in the .kanban/ folder is difficult to discover. Users must manually navigate the file system or remember file paths to find relevant docs. There is no integrated way to browse available documentation while working on tasks.
This feature adds quick sidebar access to browse all product and engineering documentation, improving discoverability and aligning with VSCode patterns where users expect sidebar trees for project navigation.

scope.in-scope: - Two new collapsible TreeView sections in the Kanban sidebar - "Product Docs" section mirroring .kanban/product/ folder hierarchy - "Engineering Docs" section mirroring .kanban/engineering/ folder hierarchy - Recursive folder traversal showing folders and .md files - Clicking a .md file opens it in the editor - FileSystemWatcher for auto-refresh when docs change - Path-based parent tracking for reveal() support
scope.out-of-scope: - Parsing markdown headers/sections (folders + files only) - Search/filter functionality within TreeView - Creating/editing docs from TreeView (use existing commands) - Syntax highlighting or preview in TreeView - Custom icons per doc type (use standard folder/file icons)

spec.requirements: - FR1: The system shall display a "Product Docs" TreeView section in the Kanban sidebar - FR2: The system shall display an "Engineering Docs" TreeView section in the Kanban sidebar - FR3: Each section shall show a tree structure mirroring the folder hierarchy of its respective directory - FR4: Folders shall be expandable/collapsible showing their contents - FR5: Markdown files (.md) shall appear as clickable leaf items - FR6: Clicking a markdown file shall open it in the editor using the kanban.openFile command - FR7: The system shall auto-refresh TreeViews when files change in the docs folders - FR8: The system shall handle missing or empty folders gracefully (return empty array) - FR9: The system shall use path-based identity for parent tracking to support reveal()

files.file: Main capability implementing TreeDataProviders for both Product and Engineering docs. Contains DocsFolderItem and DocsFileItem TreeItem classes. Uses factory DI pattern with FileSystemCapability dependency. Implements recursive folder traversal and path-based parent tracking.
Add two view declarations to contributes.views.kanban: - kanbanProductDocs with name "Product Docs" - kanbanEngineeringDocs with name "Engineering Docs"

Import and instantiate docs-view capability. Create TreeDataProviders and register TreeViews. Setup FileSystemWatchers for .kanban/product/**/*.md and .kanban/engineering/**/*.md. Connect watchers to refresh callbacks.

patterns.pattern: Create capability factory, register TreeDataProvider, register TreeView with vscode.window.createTreeView()
I/O operations in capability, pure logic separate. TreeItem classes extend vscode.TreeItem.
Factory function accepts typed DependenciesInterface, returns CreateCapabilityReturn interface.
Extend vscode.TreeItem for each node type (DocsFolderItem, DocsFileItem). Set iconPath, command, contextValue in constructor.
Use path-based identity instead of Maps. Compute parent from file path string.
Create EventEmitter, fire on changes. Return refresh callback from factory.
Reuse kanban.openFile command with filePath argument for clickable items.

research.product: - vscode/kanban-view: Core TreeView architecture with multiple sections, parent tracking pattern - docs/_index: Product docs in .kanban/product/, engineering docs in .kanban/engineering/ - docs/product: User-facing feature docs organized as {domain}/{feature}.md - docs/engineering: Technical docs organized by type: systems/, patterns/, conventions/ - vscode/file-watcher: Currently watches only task XMLs, need new watchers for docs
research.engineering: - systems/vscode-extension: Capability/Computer/Orchestrator architecture - patterns/factory-di: Factory functions with typed dependencies - patterns/capability-computer: I/O in capabilities, pure logic in computers - conventions/file-naming: kebab-case.capability.ts naming
research.codebase: - tasks-view.capability.ts: Complex TreeView with hierarchy, caching, parent tracking - config-view.capability.ts: Simple flat TreeView, good minimal example - global-actions-view.capability.ts: Collapsible group + action items pattern - file-system.capability.ts: readDir(), isDirectory(), exists() methods available - extension.ts:209-235: TreeView registration pattern - package.json:26-50: View declarations in contributes.views.kanban
research.pitfalls: - File system watching: Add separate FileSystemWatcher for docs folders (user decision) - Recursive traversal: Implement in capability with depth limiting - Parent tracking: Use path-based identity, compute parent from path string (user decision) - Performance: Filter by .md extension in code after readDir() (user decision) - Missing folders: Wrap readDir() in try-catch, return empty array on error - Empty state: Not a concern - map buttons remain visible regardless (user clarification) - Command binding: Reuse kanban.openFile command for markdown files

spec.constraints: - Must follow Capability/Computer/Orchestrator architecture (architecture directive) - Must use correct file suffixes: .capability.ts (architecture directive) - No any type - use unknown and narrow (typescript directive) - All exported functions must have explicit return types (typescript directive) - Use VSCode ThemeIcons, no hardcoded colors (design directive) - Commands accessible via command palette (design directive) - Capabilities cannot import other capabilities (architecture directive)

dependencies.internal: - FileSystemCapability: readDir(), isDirectory(), exists(), joinPath() - kanban.openFile command: existing command for opening files in editor
dependencies.external: - VSCode TreeView API: TreeDataProvider, TreeItem, createTreeView - VSCode EventEmitter: for refresh signals - VSCode FileSystemWatcher: for auto-refresh on file changes

risks.risk: Large doc hierarchies may slow initial render. Mitigation: Filter by extension in code, avoid extra stat calls.
Deeply nested folders could cause performance issues. Mitigation: Reasonable depth in practice, could add limit if needed.
